browser: The user's stable Google Chrome, driven through the official Claude in Chrome extension in its own tab-group window. Comet Catcher's earlier contract 12-13 and contract 22 runs used headless Chrome over the DevTools protocol, before the user's browser rule ruled that out. Held keys were synthetic in-page keydown/keyup events; held touch buttons were pointer events on the real touch buttons; Start, language, full-window and Play again were real mouse clicks. Only visible DOM text and canvas pixels were read; no game state was read or injected.
savedProgressSeeding: Later levels were reached by writing the host's own saved-progress preference (localStorage pixel-arcade-v1 levels[id]), which is what a returning player has.
phoneLayouts: The Chrome window could not be resized, so phone layouts were checked in a same-origin 390x844 portrait frame and an 844x390 landscape frame.

observed: A driver that follows only the status-line prompt won all 24 gardens back to back with hull 3 for 15400.
Idle play lost garden 1 with 'Night fell on garden 1 before it was restored.'; keys on the loss screen changed nothing.

Chinese portrait layout (390x844): the touch buttons alone collected the seed, planted it and restored garden 1; idle play reached the Chinese loss screen, and Play again restarted garden 1 with hull 3.
A driver that reads only the prompt and the drawn net, marker and bin arrow won contract 22 for 260: 'Every contract is fulfilled. The sky is safe!'.
A continuous run from contract 1 cleared contracts 1-3 in Chrome; headless runs advanced from contract 12 to 13.
Idle play lost in Chinese with '天文台的尝试次数用完了'; input was frozen afterwards.
Chinese landscape full-window layout (844x390): touch controls sat in side columns, and holding the right-hand touch button moved the net from the centre to the bin.
Pixel Parkour is the first card, with its gameplay picture, and the shelf count reads 39.
Clicking the card opened public/parkour/index.html?lang=zh, and the Chinese title menu ran with no console errors.

console: One exception, NotFoundError from setPointerCapture, came from a synthetic touch event with a pointer id that had no real pointer behind it; touches with a real pointer id worked. No other errors were seen.
limitations: Physical phones, touch hardware, other browsers and audio were not tested.
